page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor is equipped with a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Additionally, the hardware supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

For local storage, the instance is bundled with 472 GB of local disk capacity and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D8ds_v7 exhibits strong single-threaded performance, notably achieving a top-tier rating in bzip3 decompression at 15.08 GB/sec and a strong rating in single-threaded gzip compression at 35.05 GB/sec. Its multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth (89.09 GB/sec read and 39.04 GB/sec write for large blocks) fall within the average range. The server also demonstrates strong text generation capabilities for small language models, processing 270.06 tokens/sec on a 135M parameter model.

From a resource density perspective, the D8ds_v7 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that require a mix of compute, memory, and local storage. The inclusion of 472 GB of local storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for applications requiring fast temporary storage without the overhead of external disk attachments. This server is well-suited for relational databases, web serving, application servers, and moderate data processing tasks.
